title: Optimizer-Induced Mode Connectivity: From AdamW to Muon
claim: Solutions from the same optimizer connect along paths that preserve their spectrum, while interpolation between distinct solutions passes through a loss barrier.
layout: 2 stacked rows of 7 histograms, left-to-right, loss curve overlaid
description: Two horizontal rows of seven small singular-value histograms, one row for AdamW and one for Muon. The row labels at the ends read AdamW or Muon, and the columns between them are interpolation coefficients 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9. A thick teal curve runs across each row, with dots at each column and the eval loss written beside each dot. Loss rises from about 3.5 at the endpoints to a peak at the middle (7.90 for AdamW, 8.44 for Muon), then falls back to 3.5. The histogram bars shift from blue at the left to green at the right to show the interpolation. The AdamW histograms are sharply skewed toward zero. The Muon histograms are narrower and bell-shaped. The left axis is labeled eval loss with a downward arrow, and the bottom axis is interpolation weight with an arrow pointing right. The eye goes first to the large teal curves and the loss numbers.
caption: Motivating Experiment. Singular value histograms for layer 1 up$\_$proj weights in GPT-2 training. Models trained with AdamW and Muon converge to solutions with distinct spectrum. Solutions obtained by the same optimizer can be interpolated by paths that preserve the spectrum. Naive interpolation does not connect models with low loss paths. See [ref] for experimental details.
abstract: Mode connectivity has been widely studied, yet the role of the optimizer remains underexplored. We revisit it through optimizer-induced implicit regularization, asking how connectivity behaves when restricted to solutions constrained by a given optimizer. For two-layer ReLU networks, we show that solutions from a single optimizer -- AdamW, Muon, or others in the Lion-$\mathcal{K}$ family -- form a connected set at sufficiently large width, a result not implied by prior work. We then characterize how optimizer-induced regions interact: at large width two different regions can be disjoint or overlap depending on regularization, while in our small-width example AdamW and Muon converge to disconnected zero-loss components separated by a provable loss barrier. Empirically, in GPT-2 pretraining, we observe same-optimizer paths preserve each model's spectrum while cross-optimizer paths traverse a smooth transition. Our results reveal optimizer-dependent structure beyond classical mode connectivity literature.
